method: Each value in sha256 is the SHA-256 of a lowercase phrase of letters and digits, joined by one space or by nothing (scripts/public-identity.mjs hash). An entry marked strict is one whole word (a standalone first name) and is matched only as a complete token. Each value in starts is only the first 16 bits of the hash of a phrase's first word, a speed filter that confirms nothing by itself. The phrases themselves are deliberately not stored.
limits: Hashes of short names can be brute-forced by anyone who hashes a list of candidate names; this keeps the check from publishing the strings, not from being guessed. The check matches whole tokens and windows of up to four adjacent tokens, so a string glued to other letters or digits is not found.
